snip.t: "What are the absolute contraindications to LP?" (Signs of raised ICP, focal neurological deficits, GCS <10, new-onset seizures, coagulopathy).
ABC: intubate patients who are comatose, cannot protect their airway or have raised ICP.
The mainstay of treatment is to prevent secondary injury from hypoxia, hypotension, raised ICP, seizures, infection, hyponatraemia, hyperthermia and hypoglycaemia.
snip.s: Head Injury: Assessment, Intracranial Haematomas and Management of Raised ICP

snip.t: Papilloedema: Axoplasmic flow stasis at the optic disc from prolonged raised ICP (often absent in hyperacute presentations).
Cerebral oedema: Can progress to coma, brain herniation — Maintain normocapnia, avoid rapid Na⁺ correction, consider mannitol if signs of raised ICP
Meninges & CSF: Dura, arachnoid, pia; CSF dynamics — Headache, meningitis, raised ICP

Global symptoms: Headache (pattern, triggers), seizures, altered consciousness, fever, neck stiffness — Headache → raised ICP or meningitis; seizures → cortical irritation; fever/neck stiffness → infection
Brain parenchyma: Intracranial mass or edema → raised ICP headache
